title: fullcycle's overhead line charges the confirm prompt's wait on a person to the gate's wall
body:
## Finding

`fullcycle`'s overhead line charges a person's think-time at the confirm prompt to the gate's wall. `_fullcycle_confirm` is called from `_fullcycle_run` (`lib/cmd/fullcycle`, the `force = 0` branch), and `cmd_fullcycle` runs `_fullcycle_run` under `run_gate`. `run_gate` reaches `open_run_log`, which sets `DEVBIN_RUN_T0`, so the clock is running while `proceed? [y/N]` waits. The in-process gate keeps stdin for exactly that prompt.

Found by laksa-dc on 2026-09-03 on Laksa: paired runs, `clean rust` took 4 s with `--force` and 1 m 30 s prompted, with build and test within 6 s of each other. About 86 s of waiting on a person was reported as apparatus overhead. Re-read at HEAD by laksa-dc (a7713e5) and by dc (2026-09-21): 0089 moved the prompt to one question at the top, still inside `run_gate`, so the same wait lands in the same numerator. Not re-driven, because that needs a prompted `fullcycle`, which cleans and rebuilds.

## Why 0049 does not already cover it

0049 (closed) made the line name its numerator as the GATE's wall, with the clause "The wall covers everything this gate ran, tests or not", and left open how a gate that wraps other verbs should time itself. A person deciding is not something the gate ran, so the line is now false about its own stated subject. This issue asks only that the numerator exclude the wait. The wider 0049 question stays open and is not settled here.

## Two candidate defaults (vc to choose)

1. **Ask before the log opens:** move `_fullcycle_confirm` out of `_fullcycle_run` into `cmd_fullcycle`, ahead of `run_gate`. The answer is known before T0. Cost: the prompt and the consent notice no longer appear in the run's log, which today records what was consented to.
2. **Restart the clock after the answer:** a `runlog` helper (runlog owns T0, so fullcycle does not write the global itself) that `_fullcycle_run` calls once the prompt returns. The log keeps the consent. Cost: one more runlog entry point, and a T0 that can move after `open_run_log`, which the T0 comment currently says it cannot.

dc leans to 2, because the log records consent. No project-level override: this makes the line true, it is not a policy.

## Test

An arm driving `fullcycle` with the prompt answered after a measured delay on a stub tree, asserting the reported wall excludes the delay. Red first.

## vc's pick (2026-09-21)

Candidate 2, with one condition: the wait is RECORDED, not only subtracted. T0 restarts through the runlog-owned helper, and the log carries the consent AND the time spent waiting on it, on its own line. Excluding think-time from the overhead numerator is right; losing it without a trace would swap one false clause for a silent one. Build waits on hv's order.

## Resolution

Fixed at `1d6808b`, reviewed by vc, as vc's (a') rather than the candidate 2 picked above. **Candidate 2 could not work:** `run_gate` runs its command as `"$@" | tee -a "$log"`, so the confirm ran in a pipeline subshell, and a T0 moved there never reaches `print_run_overhead` in the parent. dc caught it before building. vc also declined a log-parsing channel (the meter would read its number out of display text any phase can imitate). So `fullcycle` now shows its notice and preview and asks BEFORE `run_gate` opens its log. `ask_person` alone is timed, and the gated run's first line records the consent and the wait: `devbin: confirmed y to clean rust --force-blocked --force at the prompt after Ns -- before this gate's wall began`. The phase and flags come from the same helpers the preview used, so the record cannot drift from what was shown. The overhead meter is unchanged, and its "covers everything this gate ran" is true again. 0088's tty rule moves to one `lib/runlog` helper, `stdin_tty_flag`, used by `run_gate` and the ask. An `n` or a missing tty now stops before any log exists. Two arms, red first (a delayed y recorded with its wait and kept out of the wall; an n leaving no gate log), plus a mutant that puts a 6 s wait back inside the gate, which reds the wall assertion. Ships in 0.1.3. 0049's wider question (per-phase T0) is untouched.
